nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ and every binary tree $T$ with keys in $\alpha$, every key of $T$ satisfies $p$ if and only if every element of the inorder traversal of $T$ satisfies $p$.
nodes.title: A predicate holds on every key iff it holds along the inorder traversal

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. For a natural number $n$ (the fuel) and a list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the tree built from $xs$ with fuel $n$ is the empty tree if $n = 0$ or $xs$ is empty. Otherwise $n = k + 1$ and $xs$ is nonempty; let $m$ be the minimum of $xs$, and let $L$ and $R$ be the parts of $xs$ before and after the first occurrence of $m$. Then the tree has root $m$, its left subtree is built from $L$ with…
nodes.title: Fuel-bounded Cartesian tree construction

nodes.summary: For a list $xs$ over a linear order, the Cartesian tree of $xs$ is the result of the fuel-bounded Cartesian tree construction on $xs$ with fuel equal to the length of $xs$. So the empty list gives the empty tree, and otherwise the root is the minimum $m$ of $xs$, the left subtree is built in the same way from the elements before the first occurrence of $m$, and the right subtree from the elements after that…
nodes.title: Cartesian tree of a list

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order, the Cartesian tree of $xs$ is min-heap ordered.
nodes.title: Cartesian trees are heap-ordered

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $\le$. A binary tree with keys in $\alpha$ is min-heap ordered when, at every node, the key $k$ of that node satisfies $k \le y$ for every key $y$ in its left subtree and every key $y$ in its right subtree. The empty tree is min-heap ordered.
nodes.title: Min-heap ordered binary tree

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order, the inorder traversal of the Cartesian tree of $xs$ is $xs$.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of a Cartesian tree

nodes.summary: For an element $a$ and a list $as$ over a linear order, the left-fold minimum of $a$ and $as$ is the minimum of the list with head $a$ and tail $as$. It is computed from the head: it equals $a$ when $as$ is empty, and when $as$ has head $b$ and tail $bs$ it equals the left-fold minimum of $\min(a, b)$ and $bs$.
nodes.title: Minimum of a nonempty list

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order and every element $x$, $x$ is a key of the Cartesian tree of $xs$ if and only if $x$ occurs in $xs$.
nodes.title: Keys of a Cartesian tree

nodes.summary: For every binary tree $T$ and every key $k$, if $T$ is nonempty with root key $k$, then $k$ is a key of $T$.
nodes.title: The root of a binary tree is one of its keys

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order, the inorder traversal of the Cartesian tree of $xs$ is a permutation of $xs$.
nodes.title: The keys of a Cartesian tree permute its input

nodes.summary: For every nonempty list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the Cartesian tree of $xs$ has a root key $m$.
nodes.title: The Cartesian tree of a nonempty list has a root

nodes.summary: Let $xs$ be a list over a linearly ordered type. If the Cartesian tree of $xs$ has root key $m$, then $m$ occurs in $xs$ and $m \le y$ for every element $y$ of $xs$.
nodes.title: The root of a Cartesian tree is a minimum of the list

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a binary tree over a preordered type that is heap-ordered (in min-heap order). If $T$ has root key $k$, then $k \le x$ for every key $x$ occurring in $T$.
nodes.title: The root of a heap-ordered tree is below every key

nodes.summary: For a binary tree $T$ with keys in $\alpha$, the root key of $T$ is an optional element of $\alpha$: it is absent (none) when $T$ is empty, and it is $k$ when the top node of $T$ holds the key $k$.
nodes.title: Optional root key of a binary tree

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an element of a type with decidable equality and let $xs$ be a list in which $m$ occurs. When $xs$ is split at the first occurrence of $m$, the left part does not contain $m$.
nodes.title: Splitting at the first occurrence leaves the value out of the left part

nodes.summary: For a value $m$ of a type with decidable equality and a list $xs$, the split of $xs$ at $m$ is the pair of the part of $xs$ before the first occurrence of $m$ and the part after it; that occurrence itself is dropped. If $m$ does not occur in $xs$, the split is the pair of $xs$ and the empty list.
nodes.title: Splitting a list at the first occurrence of a value

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
